The project's release versions, highest first (members, FR-62): in development, awaiting merge, released and imported baselines, with tag, base, branch, PR, checkpoints, the retired preset of a migrated version (history, FR-129) and dates.

post.summary: Start a new release version (Owner, FR-60, FR-61): needs a released project whose release is merged and nothing in development. The project goes to refinement / active at checkpoint 1 with the request as its idea; VERSION_STARTED is recorded and the Repository Analyst is queued. stack (FR-117, optional) is the new version's stack composition (validated like project create); omitted, the base version's composition is kept, re-pinned to the current catalog.

201.description: The release version (in_development) and the project state.

400.description: VALIDATION (version or request missing or too long), VERSION_INVALID (not MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-prerelease]), STACK_INCOMPATIBLE (violations extension) or VCS_MISMATCH.

409.description: VERSION_IN_PROGRESS, RELEASE_NOT_MERGED (the latest release is awaiting merge), NOT_RELEASED, VERSION_NOT_GREATER (not above the released version), TAG_EXISTS (the tag is already in the repository) or CONFLICT.

502.description: UPSTREAM_ERROR: the repository's tags could not be checked.

get.summary: The lifecycle checkpoints of a release version (default: the version in development, else the latest released), newest first (members, FR-44, FR-63): the phase recorded at each, when it was entered, and whether it is a rollback target now. Replaces v1's GET /versions (D-V2-11).

404.description: NOT_FOUND: the project, or a releaseVersionId of another project.

get.summary: The stack catalog (FR-113): layers, choices in evaluation order with their options (chips, description, pack, pack version, stack-packs source, modes), the compatibility rule statements and the recommended combinations, plus the catalog version and content hash.

post.summary: Option states for a partial composition (FR-114, FR-115, §4.17): every choice with each option's state (allowed, caveat, forbidden, or invalidated for a selection that earlier choices now forbid), the reasons (rule id and text), whether a recommended combination includes it, and the default to preselect.

400.description: VALIDATION: an unknown pack or option id, or a malformed layer path.

post.summary: Validate a composition (FR-116): the normalised composition with its derived fields (Next.js mode, specialists, origin model options, spec sections, env names, gates) and caveats. Left-out layers are None; the local dev loop and origin model take their defaults; vcs is required.

400.description: STACK_INCOMPATIBLE: the composition breaks a compatibility rule (the violations extension lists {layer, option, rule, reason}); VALIDATION: an unknown id, a missing vcs or a malformed path.

post.summary: Import detection (FR-118): reads the repository's file list and manifests at ref (default: the default branch) through the Git provider (github_app with the caller's GitHub connection, github_pat with an optional token, gitlab with the caller's GitLab connection on instanceId (FR-141), local under Git:Local:ImportRoot) and returns the suggested choices with their layer paths and evidence, and the conflicting ones (left empty, every candidate shown). The VCS layer is fixed to the repository's host. Nothing is stored.

400.description: VALIDATION: a malformed repo, ref or token, an instanceId or connectionId for a provider other than gitlab, or (local) a directory outside the import root or local import not enabled. GIT_HOST_NOT_ALLOWED (gitlab).

404.description: NOT_FOUND: no such repository or ref, or the caller can't see it.

409.description: GIT_NOT_CONNECTED: github_app without a valid GitHub connection, or gitlab without a valid GitLab connection on the instance.

429.description: GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED (Retry-After: seconds until GitHub's rate-limit reset)

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the action is allowed again.

502.description: UPSTREAM_ERROR: GitHub failed or couldn't be reached, or the local repository couldn't be read.

get.summary: Settings → Stack (FR-117, any member): the stack composition pinned on the current release version with its derived fields, the catalog version and hash it was pinned against (and the current ones), whether it is locked and why (plan_locked, not_in_development), the stack change against the version's base code (layersChanged, isStackChange), the retired v2 preset of a migrated version (legacyPreset, history: Preset <id>@<version> (retired, migrated)), and the VCS option fixed by the repository host (repoVcs).

put.summary: Change the stack of the version in development (Owner, FR-117): validates the composition like POST /api/stack/validate plus R5 (the VCS layer is the repository's host; omitted, it is set from it), pins it with the current catalog version and hash (a migrated version keeps its retired preset as history), updates the project's stack packs and records STACK_CHANGED {from, to, layersChanged}. The pinned composition again changes nothing. Allowed until the version's first implementation plan is locked.

400.description: STACK_INCOMPATIBLE (violations extension), VCS_MISMATCH (vcs isn't the repository's host) or VALIDATION (an unknown id or a malformed or overlapping path).

403.description: FORBIDDEN: only Owners change the stack.

409.description: STACK_LOCKED (the version's implementation plan is locked, or no version is in development) or CONFLICT (a concurrent edit).

get.summary: Admin → Stack catalog (§6): the catalog version, content hash and load status, every load error, and each pack with its stack-packs source, version, content hash and load status.
The caller's notifications, newest first, with the total unread count. unreadOnly=true lists unread ones only; load more with before = the previous page's nextBefore. limit defaults to 50 (max 100).

400.description: VALIDATION: limit out of range or before is not a nextBefore value.

get.summary: The number of the caller's unread notifications.

patch.summary: Mark one of the caller's notifications as read (idempotent: an already read notification keeps its readAt).

404.description: NOT_FOUND: no such notification for the caller.

post.summary: Mark all the caller's unread notifications as read.

204.description: Every notification of the caller is read.

get.summary: The caller's in-app notification preferences (muted types). Project channels are project settings.

put.summary: Replace the caller's muted notification types. Muted types are not added to the caller's notification centre; already created notifications are kept.

400.description: VALIDATION: an unknown type or too many entries.

get.summary: What a one-click approval link would decide (Owner of the gate's project, browser session): the gate, project, decision and gated artifact. Reading never uses the link.

401.description: UNAUTHENTICATED: sign in, then open the link again.

403.description: FORBIDDEN: the caller is not an Owner of the gate's project (or used an API token).

409.description: LINK_USED: the link was already used.

410.description: LINK_EXPIRED: the link is older than 72 hours.

200.description: The link is valid, or its gate is no longer pending (status gate_closed).

post.summary: Confirm the link's decision (Owner of the gate's project, browser session): approves or rejects the gate exactly as the gate endpoints do, and uses up the link (and its sibling link for the same gate).

401.description: UNAUTHENTICATED: sign in, then open the link again.

403.description: FORBIDDEN: the caller is not an Owner of the gate's project (or used an API token); ANTIFORGERY: missing X-XSRF-TOKEN.

409.description: LINK_USED (the link was already used), GATE_NOT_PENDING (the gate was decided or cancelled elsewhere) or CONFLICT (a concurrent change).

410.description: LINK_EXPIRED: the link is older than 72 hours.

ActivityItemDto.description:
One entry of a project's activity feed (FR-50). `type` is the stored event type (e.g. `PHASE_CHANGED`),
`category` its feed category (`null` for internal events), `summary` a one-line description and
`payload` the raw event payload.

ActivityPageDto.description: A page of the activity feed, newest first. Pass `nextBefore` as `before` to load more; `null` when there is no more.

ActorDto.description: Who did something: a user (`id` and display name) or the system actor (`isSystem`, no `id`).

AddMemberRequest.description: Adds an existing user by email (FR-8).

AdminAgentRunDto.description:
One agent run in the cross-project admin run log (FR-23, FR-51): the project, agent, phase, step, provider, model,
prompt template version, status, provider attempts, token counts, estimated cost in USD, duration and error. Input
artifacts, feedback and output are on the project's run detail (`GET /api/projects/{id}/runs/{runId}`).

AdminBitbucketIntegrationDto.description:
Admin → Integrations → Bitbucket (FR-133): the OAuth consumer and its registration help. `callbackUrl` is the exact
callback to enter on the consumer (`App:PublicBaseUrl` + `/api/auth/bitbucket/callback`); `permissions` are
the consumer permissions to tick (`account email repository:write repository:admin pullrequest:write project
webhook`; Bitbucket fixes scopes on the consumer). `source` is `configuration` when
`Bitbucket__OAuth__*` sets the consumer (then it can't be changed or removed here). The secret is a flag only
(`hasClientSecret`). `oauthConfigured`: key and secret are set, so "Continue with Bitbucket" and OAuth
connections work (API-token connections work without). `connectionCount` counts users' Bitbucket connections.

AdminEventDto.description:
One entry of the cross-project admin event log (FR-51). `projectId`/`projectName` are `null` for events
without a project (e.g. `PROJECT_DELETED`, whose project id is in the payload). `type` is the stored event
type, `category` its activity-feed category (`null` for operations markers such as
`DEAD_LETTER_RETRIED`), `outcome` whether it records a failure or alert, `summary` a one-line
description and `payload` the raw event payload.

AdminGitHubAppDto.description:
The AIDE GitHub App's status for Admin → Integrations → GitHub (FR-80). Secrets (client secret, private key) are never
returned. `source` is `configuration` when `GitHub__App__*` is set (it takes precedence), `database`
for an App registered through the manifest flow, and `null` when `status` is `not_configured` (then every
App field is `null` and `permissions` is empty). `installUrl` is
`https://github.com/apps/{slug}/installations/new`; `permissions` are the App's granted permissions
(e.g. `contents: write`); `canCreateRepositories` is true when `administration: write` is granted (§4.14).
`pagesPermission` (FR-143) is `granted` when the App has `pages: write`, `missing` for an App registered
before v4 ("Pages permission missing: update the App's permissions in GitHub, then accept them on each installation"),
and `unknown` when the App isn't configured or GitHub couldn't be asked.

AdminGitLabInstanceDto.description:
A GitLab instance for Admins (FR-130). Secrets are flags only (`hasClientSecret`). `baseUrl` is the effective
base URL (`https://gitlab.com` for gitlab.com). `source` is `configuration` when
`GitLab__Instances__<n>__*` sets it (then only `enabled` can be changed here, and it can't be removed).
`oauthConfigured`: client id and secret are set, so "Continue with GitLab" and OAuth connections work (token connections
work without). `version` is from the last reachability check (`null` when GitLab answered 401 unauthenticated);
`versionStatus` is `supported` (17.11+), `old` (with `versionWarning`) or `unknown`.
`connectionCount`/`projectCount` are the users' connections and the projects using it (removal is refused
while `projectCount` > 0).

AdminGitLabIntegrationDto.description:
Admin → Integrations → GitLab (FR-130): the registration help and the instances. `callbackUrl` is the exact redirect
URI to register on every GitLab OAuth application (`App:PublicBaseUrl` + `/api/auth/gitlab/callback`);
`scopes` are the scopes to tick (`api write_repository openid profile email`); `minimumVersion` is
`17.11`; `allowPrivateNetworks` is `GitLab:AllowPrivateNetworks` (read-only configuration). gitlab.com is
always listed first.

AdminLlmPolicyDto.description:
§2 Admin: the system LLM key policy (D-V2-5). `allowSystemKeys` is `Llm:AllowSystemKeys` (configuration,
read-only here: set `Llm__AllowSystemKeys` in `secrets.env` / user-secrets and restart). When it is on,
projects with no bound connection use the system key of their provider; `systemKeyProviders` lists the
providers that have one configured (allowed or not). Keys are never returned. Providers disabled on this deployment
(FR-157) are never listed.

AdminStackCatalogDto.description:
Admin → Stack catalog (§6 `GET /api/admin/stack`): the catalog version and hash, whether it loaded (`loaded`
or `failed`), every load error, and each pack with its source, version, hash and load status.

AdminStackPackDto.description: A pack folder: what its `pack.json` says (when readable), the SHA-256 of its files, and `loaded`/`failed` with the reasons.

AdminUserDto.description: A user as shown on the admin users page.

AdvancePhaseRequest.description: "Advance to next phase" (FR-12). `reason` is recorded on the state transition.

AdvanceResultDto.description:
Result of "advance to next phase" (FR-12). When the approval mode requires a gate for the next phase (§4.2),
`gate` is the pending gate that was created and `state` still shows the current phase; otherwise
`gate` is `null` and `state` shows the new phase.

AdvisorFindingDto.description: A Supabase security advisor finding recorded on a run (FR-153).

AgentKind.description: The cognitive agents (§1, FR-23), plus the Repository Analyst (FR-70).

AgentModelsDto.description: Model id per agent; an omitted or `null` agent uses the default model.

AgentRunDetailDto.description:
An agent run with the provider's output text (FR-23). `output` is `null` until the run succeeds and is cut
to the first 200,000 characters (`outputTruncated`). The v2 fields are as on AgentRunDto.
`toolCalls` is the run's repo tool log (FR-71: tool, arguments, bytes, truncated, error code) and `warnings`
what was recorded on it (FR-70, FR-71): `tools_unsupported`, `snapshot_unavailable`,
`summary_wait_timeout`, `summary_unavailable`, and `output_truncated` (FR-162). `continuations` is how
many continuations the answer took (0–5, FR-162) and `maxOutputTokens` the output token limit its calls used
(FR-160); both are `null` for runs stored before v4 and for runs that haven't succeeded.

AgentRunDto.description:
An agent run (FR-23): which agent ran in which phase (and step), on which provider and model, with which prompt
template version and input artifact versions; its status, provider attempts (FR-25), token counts, estimated cost in
USD, duration and error. `userFeedback` is the feedback or answers given to the agent. `releaseVersionId` is the
release version it ran for (§4.10). `checkpoint` is the checkpoint it ran at (null until recorded). `agentKey`
is the specialist that ran a plan step (FR-121; `generalist` for a generalist step of a composed project; null for
base agents); `presetId`/`presetVersion` are history (FR-129: the retired preset of runs before the upgrade).
`legacyAgentKey` (§4.23) is the v2 agent key the run's step was planned with when it ran as its mapped v4
specialist (e.g. `db-engineer` for `data-engineer`); null otherwise. `toolCallCount` is
the number of repo tool calls (FR-71). `credentialLabel` names the LLM connection that paid for the run,
`Label (••••a1b2)` (FR-79, D-V2-5; null for a system key, a provider without a key, or a deleted connection).

AgentRunStatus.description: Status of an agent run (FR-23, FR-25).

ApiTokenDto.description: A personal API token as listed (never includes the token or its hash).

ApprovalArtifactSummaryDto.description: The artifact a gate approves (spec and plan gates); `title` is its first heading, when it has one.

ApprovalLinkDecision.description: The decision a one-click approval link carries (FR-48).

ApprovalLinkStatus.description:
The state of a one-click approval link (FR-48). A 200 from `GetApprovalLink` carries `valid` (the link can
be confirmed) or `gate_closed` (the gate was decided or cancelled elsewhere; confirming answers
`GATE_NOT_PENDING`). `expired` and `used` name the states behind `LINK_EXPIRED` (410) and
`LINK_USED` (409), which are returned as ProblemDetails.

ApprovalLinkViewDto.description:
What the approval confirmation page shows (FR-48): the gate, its project, the decision the link carries and, for spec
and plan gates, the gated artifact. One-click links exist only for spec_approval, plan_approval and pre_release gates.

ArtifactAuthorDto.description:
Who produced an artifact version (FR-16): a user (`user`, for drafts edited in the browser or uploaded via the
CLI) or an agent run (`agentRunId`). Exactly one of the two is set.

ArtifactDiffDto.description:
A line diff between versions `from` and `to` of one artifact type (FR-21): `unifiedDiff` is the
unified-diff text (3 lines of context) and `lines` the same hunks as context/added/removed lines, with each
unchanged run outside them collapsed into one `skipped` entry, for side-by-side rendering. Versions with more
than 100,000 lines together are not diffed (400 `VALIDATION`).

ArtifactDto.description:
One artifact version with its Markdown content (FR-16, §4.3). `contentHash` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the
normalised content; `integrity` is `corrupted` when it no longer matches (FR-20). `approvedBy` and
`approvedAt` are set once approved (status `locked`); `rejectionComment` once rejected (FR-17).
`releaseVersionId` and `checkpointAtCreation` say where it was created (§4.10; D-V2-11: was
`projectVersionAtCreation`); `releaseVersion` is that release version's semver (FR-59).
`restoredFromVersion` is the version whose content a restore copied (FR-58), else `null`.
`warnings` are non-blocking findings about the version (FR-76, §4.13): for an `implementation_plan`,
`UNCOVERED_REQUIREMENTS` when its steps' `covers` miss a `[new]`/`[changed]` requirement of the
release version's locked specification (`ids` lists them); empty otherwise.

ArtifactIntegrity.description:
Result of re-checking an artifact's content hash on read (FR-20). `corrupted` means the stored content no
longer matches `content_hash` (§4.3), or the row is already marked ArtifactStatus.Corrupted.

ArtifactStateDto.description: Latest and current locked version of one artifact type (§6 project state).

ArtifactSummaryDto.description:
One artifact version without its content (FR-16, FR-21, FR-59): the artifacts page cards and the history list.
`integrity` is the result of re-checking the content hash on this read (FR-20); `releaseVersionId` is the
release version it belongs to (§4.10) and `releaseVersion` its semver (FR-59). `restoredFromVersion` is the
version whose content a restore copied (FR-58), else `null`.

ArtifactWarningDto.description: A non-blocking finding about an artifact version (FR-76, §4.13): its code, a message and the ids it is about.

AuthProvidersDto.description:
Which sign-in providers are available (the frontend hides "Continue with GitHub" when `github` is false).
`githubMode` (D-V2-7) says how GitHub sign-in works: `app` (the AIDE GitHub App's user authorization flow
with PKCE), `oauth` (the v1 OAuth App, only while no App is registered) or `none`; `github` is
`githubMode != none`. `gitlab` (FR-131) lists the enabled GitLab instances with an OAuth application: one
"Continue with GitLab" button each (`GET /api/auth/gitlab/start` with `instanceId` and `mode=signin`).
`bitbucket` (FR-134) is true when a Bitbucket OAuth consumer is configured: "Continue with Bitbucket"
(`GET /api/auth/bitbucket/start?mode=signin`) and OAuth connect are offered.

BitbucketConnectionDto.description:
A Bitbucket connection of the caller (FR-134); never a token or the API token's email. `externalUserId` is the
Bitbucket account UUID. `authKind` is `oauth` or `token` (Atlassian API token); `scopes` as granted
(OAuth) or as checked (API token). `status`: `valid`, `invalid` (Bitbucket rejected it; reconnect) or
`insufficient_scope`.

BitbucketOwnersDto.description:
Where the caller can create a Bitbucket repository (FR-135): their first 50 workspaces with their projects;
`truncated` says the caller has more workspaces than are listed.

BitbucketPendingLinkDto.description:
FR-134 sign-in: Bitbucket's verified email belongs to an existing AIDE account that isn't linked to this Bitbucket
identity. AIDE never links silently (D-V4-18): the user signs in to that account (any method) and confirms with
`POST /api/auth/bitbucket/link`, or cancels with `DELETE /api/auth/bitbucket/link`. Expires after 10 minutes.

BitbucketProjectDto.description: A project in a workspace (FR-135); pass `key` as `project` when creating a repository.

BitbucketRepoDto.description:
A Bitbucket repository for the repo picker (FR-135). `id` is Bitbucket's repository UUID; `fullName` is
`workspace/slug`; `mainBranch` is `null` for an empty repository.

BitbucketRepoPageDto.description:
One page of repositories (one workspace at a time, most recently updated first); pass `nextCursor` as
    `cursor` for the next (`null` = last page).

BitbucketRepoRefsDto.description:
What the wizard needs about a picked Bitbucket repository (FR-141, FR-86): its `workspace/slug`, default branch
(`mainbranch.name`), whether it is `empty` (no commits, or only starter files), its tags (Bitbucket has no
Releases, D-V4-7), and the import's suggestion: the released version to preselect (the highest semver tag; `null` =
"Never released") and the version to develop it prefills (its next minor, else `0.1.0`).

BitbucketTagDto.description: A semver-or-other tag of a Bitbucket repository; `semver` is its version (the `v` prefix stripped), or `null`.

BitbucketWorkspaceDto.description:
A workspace the caller can access (FR-135) with the first 100 of its projects (`projectsTruncated`: it has more).
Pass `slug` as `owner` when creating. `isAdmin` is whether the caller administers the workspace, when
Bitbucket says.

CategoryScoreDto.description:
One compliance category (§4.7): its weight, the agent's score (0–1), the deterministic penalty (sum of the fixed
critical/major/minor penalties of its deterministic violations) and the final score (agent score − penalty, floored
at 0), with the agent's evidence.

CheckRunDto.description:
FR-84, FR-85: a check run or commit status on the PR head. `conclusion` is set once `status` is
`completed` (else `null`). `required` is true when the default branch's rules require it.
`detailsUrl` links the check on GitHub (or the CI provider), when known.

CheckRunStatus.description: FR-84, FR-85: a GitHub check run's (or commit status's) state. Wire values `queued`, `in_progress`, `completed`.

CheckpointDto.description:
A lifecycle checkpoint of a release version (FR-44, FR-63), for the rollback target picker: the phase entered at that
checkpoint and when. `rollbackAllowed` says whether it is a valid rollback target now; when it isn't,
`rollbackBlockedReason` says why (`current_checkpoint`, `release_phase`, or `version_released` for
every checkpoint of a released version). Rate limits and running work (RATE_LIMITED, ROLLBACK_BLOCKED) are checked when
the rollback is requested.

CodebaseSummaryState.description:
The Repository Analyst's progress for a release version as shown on the Refinement page (FR-70): `not_needed` (no
existing code), `queued`, `running`, `completed` (the summary exists), `failed` (the analyst ended
without a summary) or `timed_out` (still unfinished 10 minutes after the version started; refinement no longer
waits for it).

CodebaseSummaryStatusDto.description:
FR-70: the Repository Analyst for the release version. `status`: `not_needed` (no existing code),
`queued`, `running`, `completed` (the locked summary exists: `artifactId`/`artifactVersion`),
`failed` (the analyst ended without one) or `timed_out` (unfinished 10 minutes after the version started;
refinement no longer waits). `runId` is the analyst's agent run once it has started (the run that wrote the
summary when completed), else `null`.

ComplianceDriftDto.description: The drift level and areas of the latest compliance report (FR-41, §4.7).

ComplianceReportDetailDto.description:
The full compliance report of one review cycle (FR-56): the category breakdown, every violation with its evidence,
the deterministic findings alone (`deterministicFindings`, the violations whose source is `deterministic`),
missing features, drift areas, the decision and its `escalationReason`, regressions (§4.13), the external checks
collected (FR-85 check runs, preview deployment; `null` when none), the optimisation plan it produced and
`executionRunId`, the review-fix run that plan produced (the plan artifact id, see `ListExecutionRuns`).

ComplianceReportDto.description:
The compliance report of one review cycle (FR-38, FR-41). `overallScore` is Σ category score × weight (3 dp);
`threshold` is the project's compliance threshold. `decision` follows §4.5; `decisionReason` is set
when the decision is `escalation_required` (`low_score`, `severe_drift`, `max_cycles`,
`no_improvement` or `no_optimization_plan` — another cycle was required but the review proposed no
optimisation steps), else `null`. `optimizationPlanArtifactId` is the optimisation plan draft the review
produced (FR-40), if any.

ComplianceReportSummaryDto.description:
One review cycle in the Review page's cycle list (FR-56): cycle number, overall score against the threshold it was
decided on, drift level, decision, date, the checkpoint it ran at and its release version. `id` is the report id:
cycle numbers restart after a rollback, so one release version can list two reports of the same cycle.

ComplianceTrendDto.description: The compliance score across review cycles, oldest first (FR-41), with the project's threshold. Empty before the first review.

ComplianceTrendPointDto.description:
One review cycle's result in the compliance trend (FR-41). `threshold` is the compliance threshold that cycle was
decided against (the report's snapshot; the project's threshold may have changed since).

ComponentProductionUrlDto.description:
FR-151: the production URL of one component on the project overview: its platform, the URL (`null` until known)
and the deployment production serves now (`null` before the first ready production deployment).

ConfirmApprovalLinkRequest.description: Confirms the decision of a one-click approval link; `comment` is optional (feedback on reject).

expiresAt.description: Optional expiry; must be in the future.

baseVersion.description:
The version the edit started from. When set, the save is refused with 409 `CONFLICT` (details
`latestVersion: N`) unless it is still the latest version of the type, so a version saved meanwhile is
never silently superseded. Omit it to always save (CLI uploads).

CreateArtifactDraftRequest.description: A new draft version of an artifact type from edited Markdown (FR-18).

CreateBitbucketRepoRequest.description:
Create a Bitbucket repository (FR-135) with the caller's connection `connectionId` in workspace `owner` and
project `project` (its key; Bitbucket requires one). The slug is Bitbucket's slug of `name`. AIDE then pushes an
initial commit with a README to `main`, so the default branch exists. `private` defaults to true.

CreateBitbucketTokenConnectionRequest.description:
FR-134 token fallback: an Atlassian API token with the scopes `read:user`, `read:workspace`,
`read:project`, `read:repository`, `write:repository`, `admin:repository`, `read:pullrequest`,
`write:pullrequest` and `read:pipeline` (all `:bitbucket`), and the Atlassian account `email` it
belongs to. App passwords aren't supported. Nothing is saved unless the token passes the checks.

CreateDeploymentResourceRequest.description: FR-144: create a platform resource: its name (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`), and region and plan where the platform has them.

CreateGitHubAppManifestRequest.description:
Start the GitHub App manifest flow (FR-80): the App is owned by the Admin's personal account (`user`) or by the
organisation `org` (required for `organization`, ignored for `user`).

CreateGitHubRepoRequest.description:
Create a repository (FR-81, §4.14) for `owner` (the caller's login or an organisation where the App is installed),
initialised with a README so the default branch exists.

CreateGitLabInstanceRequest.description:
Add a self-managed GitLab instance (FR-130). `baseUrl` must be `https://` (or `http://` with
`allowInsecureHttp`); it is normalised, checked by the SSRF guard (§8) and probed with `GET /api/v4/version`.
gitlab.com is always listed already (edit it to add its OAuth application). `clientId`/`clientSecret` are the
GitLab OAuth application's id and secret (optional: token connections work without).

CreateGitLabRepoRequest.description:
Create a GitLab project (FR-132) with the caller's connection `connectionId`, in namespace `owner` (a
`fullPath` from the owners list), initialised with a README so `main` exists and is the default branch.
`path` defaults to GitLab's slug of `name`. `private` (default true) sets visibility private, else public.

CreateGitLabTokenConnectionRequest.description:
FR-131 token fallback: a personal, project or group access token with `api` and `write_repository` for the
instance (`instanceId` omitted = gitlab.com). Validated with `GET /api/v4/user` and
`GET /api/v4/personal_access_tokens/self`; nothing is saved unless it passes.

CreateLlmCredentialRequest.description:
Add an LLM connection (FR-78): `anthropic` or `openai`, a label and the key. The key is checked with
    the provider before anything is saved.

name.description: The resource name; defaults to the project's name (Render preview: `<name>-preview`).

CreateManagedDatabaseRequest.description: FR-152: provision a database: region (Supabase: a region code or americas/emea/apac; Render: defaults to the backend's), plan, and an optional name.

CreatePlatformConnectionRequest.description:
Add a platform connection (FR-142, §4.20): the provider, a label and the pasted token, plus optionally the account it
is for (`accountId`: a team, account, workspace or organisation id the token reaches; required for a Railway
workspace token, which can't name its workspace itself). The token is checked with the platform before anything is
saved.

CreateProjectDeploymentRequest.description:
Deployment step of the new-project wizard (FR-88): `provider` `vercel`, one of the caller's own Vercel
connections, and an existing Vercel project (`vercelProjectId`) or a new one (`create`), not both. Needs a
GitHub-backed project (`git.mode` `local`: 400 `VALIDATION`).

installationId.description: `github_app`: the App installation that grants access to the repo (from the repo picker).

repoFullName.description:
`github_app`: the repository as `owner/name`. `gitlab`: its `group/sub/project` path (the
    stored path is the one GitLab reports for `repoId`). `bitbucket`: its `workspace/slug` (the stored one
    is what Bitbucket reports for `repoId`).

instanceId.description:
`gitlab` (FR-132, FR-136): the GitLab instance of the repository (from the repo picker). Required with gitlab and
not used otherwise (400 `VALIDATION`).

connectionId.description:
`gitlab`, `bitbucket` (FR-136): one of the caller's own valid GitLab connections on `instanceId`, or
Bitbucket connections, bound to the project: all background Git work uses it. Another user's connection is 403
`CREDENTIAL_NOT_OWNER`; a missing one 404 `NOT_FOUND`; an invalid one or a disabled instance 409
`GIT_NOT_CONNECTED`; a connection on another instance 400 `VALIDATION`. Not used with other modes.

repoId.description:
`gitlab` (FR-132): GitLab's project id; `bitbucket` (FR-135): the repository UUID (`{…}`); both from
the repo picker. The caller needs GitLab Developer access or higher, or Bitbucket `write`/`admin`, on it
(403 `FORBIDDEN`; 404 `NOT_FOUND` when the connection can't see it). Not used with other modes.

token.description: GitHub access token (`github_pat` only). Stored encrypted and never returned.

localSourcePath.description:
FR-73, §8 Testing: `local` + `source: import` only, and only where the server sets `Git:Local:ImportRoot`
(Development and E2E): the existing Git repository directory to import, absolute or relative to that root, which it
must resolve under (else 400 `VALIDATION` on `git.localSourcePath`). Omit it otherwise.

CreateProjectGitRequest.description:
Repository step of the new-project wizard (FR-5, FR-35, FR-82, FR-86). `mode` picks the Git provider.
`github_app`: a repo picked or created through the AIDE GitHub App; send `installationId` and
`repoFullName` (`owner/name`), no `repoUrl` or `token` (409 `GITHUB_APP_NOT_INSTALLED` when the
App can't access the repo). `github_pat`: `repoUrl` plus an optional `token` (FR-83, the v1 behaviour).
`local`: no remote. `provider` is the v1 name of `mode`, kept so v1 clients work: send one of the two;
when both are sent they must be equal (else 400 `VALIDATION` on `git.mode`).

CreateProjectImportRequest.description:
FR-73: the versions of an imported repository. `releasedTag` is the tag of the currently released version, picked
from the repository's GitHub Releases and semver tags (`null` or omitted: "Never released"); it must exist in the
repository (400 `TAG_NOT_FOUND`) and name a semver version (400 `VERSION_INVALID`). `developmentVersion`
is the version to develop (semver, a leading `v` is stripped; 400 `VERSION_INVALID`), greater than the
released one (409 `VERSION_NOT_GREATER`).

CreateProjectLlmRequest.description:
FR-159: the LLM choice of a new project. `provider` must be enabled and usable by the caller (else 400
`LLM_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`). `credentialId` binds one of the caller's own connections for that provider, as
`PATCH …/settings/llm` does (FR-79: 403 `CREDENTIAL_NOT_OWNER` for another user's, 404 `NOT_FOUND` for an
unknown one, 400 `VALIDATION` for one of another provider); omitted, a provider that needs a key and has no usable
system key is bound to the caller's newest connection for it. `defaultModel` is required (400 `VALIDATION`
when blank) and need not be in the catalog. `modelsByAgent` overrides models per agent; omitted, the provider's
configured per-agent defaults apply.

tokenBudget.description: Token budget (at least 1000); `null` or omitted means unlimited.

initialVersion.description:
FR-66 (`source: scratch` only): the first release version (semver, a leading `v` is stripped; default
`0.1.0`). The first release tags it.

source.description:
FR-73: `scratch` (default) starts from scratch with `initialVersion`; `import` imports the existing
repository named by `git` with `import` (required) and `idea` as the request for the version to develop.

oneOf.description: FR-73: required with `source: import`, not allowed otherwise.

FR-114, FR-115, FR-117 (wizard Stack step): the stack composition, validated like `POST /api/stack/validate`
(400 `STACK_INCOMPATIBLE` with `violations`; `VALIDATION` on `stack.*` fields) plus R5: the VCS
layer is the repository's host (GitHub for `github_app`/`github_pat`; omitted, it is set from it; another
one is 400 `VCS_MISMATCH`). It is pinned with the catalog version and hash on the version to develop. Omitted or
`null`: no stack ("No stack (general)"). FR-129: the v2 `presetId` was removed (D-V4-4).

FR-88 (wizard Deployment step): deploy to Vercel with one of the caller's own Vercel connections, linking an existing
Vercel project or creating one; omitted or `null` = no deployment (it can be set later in Settings →
Deployment). Needs a GitHub-backed project (400 `VALIDATION` on `deployment.provider` for Local).

FR-159 (wizard Configuration step, AI model section): the project's LLM provider, connection and models. Omitted or
`null`: the default for the caller (§4.24: the configured default provider if enabled and usable, else the first
enabled usable one in the order anthropic, openai, ollama, fake; 400 `LLM_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` when none is).

CreateProjectRequest.description: The new-project wizard (FR-5). Omitted settings take the FR-5 defaults.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, up to 100, without `---`.

rootDirectory.description: The app's directory in the repository (default `.`).

CreateVercelProjectRequest.description: FR-88: create a new Vercel project linked to the GitHub repo (framework `nextjs`).

CreatedApiTokenDto.description: A newly created token. string CreatedApiTokenDto.Token is shown once and can't be retrieved again.

DatabaseProvisioningDto.description:
FR-152: the `database_provisioning` job of a database card: `state` (`queued`, `running`,
`succeeded`, `failed`), the current `step` (`queued`, `creating`, `linking`,
`waiting`, `syncing_env`), and on failure the error code (`DATABASE_PROVISIONING_FAILED`,
`DATABASE_PROVISIONING_TIMEOUT`, `PLATFORM_PLAN_LIMIT`, `CREDENTIAL_INVALID`,
`CONNECTION_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT`, `UPSTREAM_ERROR`, `VALIDATION`) and message.

DeadLetterDto.description:
A dead-lettered job (FR-51, §4.9): its type, project, status (`dead`, or `retried` once an Admin retried
it), attempts made, last error and payload; `deadLetteredAt` is when it ran out of attempts.

DecideArtifactRequest.description: Approve or reject a draft (FR-17). On reject, `comment` is recorded and fed to the re-run agent.

DecideGateRequest.description:
Approve or reject a pending gate (FR-13, FR-14). `comment` is optional (on reject it is the feedback for the
re-run agent). Escalation gates are approved with a `decision`; `rollback` also needs a
`targetCheckpoint` (a checkpoint of the release version in development). Other gates take neither (400 `INVALID_DECISION`), and escalation gates can't be rejected.

DeclaredFileDto.description:
A file a step declares it creates or modifies (FR-29). `protected` marks a protected path (§4.6: .git/, .aide/, CI
workflows, lockfiles, .env files) — only an Owner-edited plan can declare one; the step may then write it.

DeploymentBuildConfigDto.description: The build configuration AIDE derived from the composition (§4.20); each field is `null` when it doesn't apply.

DeploymentComponent.description: A deployable component of a project (FR-144). Wire values: `frontend`, `backend`.

DeploymentDatabaseDto.description:
FR-152 database card (Settings → Deployment `databases[]`, one per environment when the composition has a
database host or a database is set): `provider` (`supabase`, `render`, `railway`, `external`,
`fake`), `status` (`not_configured`, `provisioning`, `available`, `error`, `paused`,
`expiring`, `removed`), the composition's `hostOption`, the binding ("connected by"), the resource, region,
plan, expiry, the dashboard link (`resourceUrl`), a connection summary without secrets (host, port, database), the
Supabase permissions the connection lacks (e.g. "API Key Secrets: Read"), the provisioning job, and `warnings`
(`render_free_expiry`, `supabase_free_pausing`, `supabase_free_project_limit`,
`preview_uses_production_database`). Secrets are never returned.

DeploymentDto.description:
A preview or production deployment (FR-90, FR-91, §4.15). `status` follows `queued → building → ready | error |
canceled`. `url` is the deployment URL once known, `inspectorUrl` Vercel's inspector page. `gitRef`
and `gitSha` are what was deployed; `releaseVersion` is the version (e.g. `1.2.0`) of
`releaseVersionId`; `releaseId` is the release attempt of a production deployment (`null` for previews).
A failed deployment carries `errorCode` (`PLATFORM_ERROR`, formerly `VERCEL_ERROR`; `DEPLOYMENT_TIMEOUT`), `errorMessage` and
`buildLogTail` (the end of the build log). `trigger` is `auto` (AIDE, after execution or the release
merge), `manual`, `promote` or `redeploy`; `triggeredBy` is `null` for `auto` (or a
deleted user). `promotedFromDeploymentId` is the earlier production deployment a `promote` (or
`rollback`) row made current again.
FR-150, FR-151: `component` (`frontend`, `backend`), `kind` (`deploy`, `rollback`,
`promote`), `platform` (the target's host; `provider` is `fake` in Fake mode), `current` (the
deployment production serves now, per component), `canRollback` with `rollbackBlockedReason` when false
(`unsupported`, `not_production`, `not_ready`, `unknown_at_platform`, `current`), and
`olderThanLatestMigration` (the rollback dialog's database warning; `null` = unknown, until M30 databases).

DeploymentEnvInventoryDto.description: The environment inventory (FR-145): the frontend pack's public prefix (`NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `VITE_`, or `null`) and the rows.

DeploymentEnvSource.description:
Who wrote an environment variable (FR-145). Wire values: `user`, `derived`; `required` is an
            inventory row only (a pack's required variable without a value), never stored.

DeploymentEnvVarDto.description:
One row of the environment inventory (FR-145): `key`, the components it applies to, its environments, whether it is
sensitive or public, its `source` (`user`, `derived`, `required`), what a derived one comes from
(`derivedFrom`), a required one's `description`, `hasValue` (required rows and derived rows without a
source URL yet: `false`; values are never returned), and the sync state (`syncedAt`, `syncError`).

DeploymentEnvironment.description:
Deployment environment (FR-147, FR-149), also a Vercel env target (FR-88). Wire values: `preview`,
            `production`.

DeploymentKind.description: What a deployment row does (FR-150, §5). Wire values: `deploy`, `rollback`, `promote`.

DeploymentOriginModelDto.description:
FR-146: the composition's origin model (`same-origin`, `proxy`, `cross-origin`; `null` API only), the
stack-packs vocabulary's (`packModel`: `same-origin` or `cross-origin`), the models the Owner may switch
between (Settings → Stack) and the one-line explanation.

DeploymentProvider.description:
Deployment provider (§4.15, §4.20): a target's platform, from the composition's host (`deploy-vercel` → `vercel`).
Wire values: `vercel`, `fake` (v2's explicit Fake provider; deployments made under
`Deployments:Provider=Fake` are recorded as `fake`), `netlify`, `cloudflare`, `render`,
`railway`, `github_pages`.

DeploymentSettingsDto.description:
Settings → Deployment (FR-144, any member; D-V4-4 replaced v2's single Vercel shape): `targets`, `databases`,
the environment inventory (`env`; keys only) and the `originModel`. `canManage`: the caller is an Owner.
`fakeMode`: `Deployments:Provider=Fake`.

DeploymentSetupDto.description:
The `deployment_setup` job of a target (FR-144): `state` `queued`, `running`, `succeeded` or
`failed`; `step` while it runs (`queued`, `creating`, `linking`, `syncing_env`); when it
failed, `errorCode` (`PLATFORM_GIT_NOT_CONNECTED`, `PLATFORM_PLAN_LIMIT`, `PLATFORM_PERMISSION_MISSING`,
`CREDENTIAL_INVALID`, `NOT_FOUND`, `VALIDATION`, `PLATFORM_ERROR`, `UPSTREAM_ERROR`), the
`message` and a `fixUrl` (the platform's install or connect link, or the GitHub App settings).

DeploymentStatus.description: §4.15 deployment states: `queued → building → ready | error | canceled`.

DeploymentTargetBindingDto.description:
A target's bound connection (FR-144): which of the binder's platform connections, "connected by <name>", the
account it reaches and its status. Never the token.

DeploymentTargetDto.description:
One target card of Settings → Deployment (FR-144): one per component whose host the composition names (plus a target
set up before the composition dropped its host, `inComposition: false`). `provider` is the composition's host
(`hostOption` is its catalog id). `binding` is the bound connection (`null` for GitHub Pages, which uses
the project's GitHub App or PAT) and `needsConnection` whether one is needed; `canBind` whether the caller may
bind one of their own. `resourceId`/`name` the platform resource (`null` until set up),
`rootDirectory` and `buildConfig` what it builds, the production and preview URLs once known, `status`
(`not_configured`, `configuring`, `ready`, `attention`, `error`) with `statusReason`, the
setup job (`setup`, `null` before the first), the provider's capabilities and the readiness checklist
(platform items say "not checked yet" until `verify`). `fakeMode`: deployments run on the Fake provider.

DeploymentTargetStatus.description:
State of a deployment target (FR-144). Wire values: `not_configured`, `configuring`, `ready`,
            `attention`, `error`.

DeploymentTrigger.description:
Why a deployment row exists (FR-90, FR-91). Wire values: `auto` (AIDE after execution or release),
            `manual`, `promote`, `redeploy`.

DeploymentUserDto.description: A user named on a deployment or binding: "connected by <name>", "triggered by <name>".

DeploymentVerifyDto.description: FR-144: the readiness checklist of `POST …/targets/:component/verify`, with the target after the check.

token.description: `github_pat` only: the GitHub token to read a private repository. Used for this request only, never stored.

connectionId.description:
`gitlab` or `bitbucket` (FR-141): one of the caller's connections for that host (GitLab: on the instance;
404 `NOT_FOUND` otherwise). Omitted: the caller's newest valid one. Not used with other providers (400).

DetectStackGitRequest.description:
FR-118: where the repository is. `provider`: `github_app` (`repo` = `owner/name`, read with the
caller's GitHub connection: 409 `GIT_NOT_CONNECTED` without one), `github_pat` (`repo` = `owner/name`
or `https://github.com/owner/name`, with the optional `token`; public repositories need none) or `local`
(`repo` = the directory under `Git:Local:ImportRoot`, Development and E2E only). `ref` is the branch, tag
or commit to read (default: the default branch). FR-141: `gitlab` (`repo` = GitLab's project id or its
`group/sub/project` path) on `instanceId` (omitted: gitlab.com), read with the caller's `connectionId` or,
omitted, their newest valid GitLab connection on that instance (409 `GIT_NOT_CONNECTED` without one).
`instanceId` and `connectionId` are only for gitlab (400 `VALIDATION` otherwise).

DetectStackRequest.description: FR-118: the repository to detect the stack of.

DiffLineDto.description:
One line of a diff between two versions (FR-21). `oldLine` is the 1-based line number in the `from` version
(null for `added`), `newLine` the line number in the `to` version (null for `removed`); `text`
is the line without its line ending. Lines are in order, so a side-by-side view pairs them by line numbers.
A `skipped` entry stands for `skipped` unchanged lines (more than 3 lines from any change) that are left
out: `oldLine`/`newLine` are the numbers of the first of them and `text` is empty; `skipped` is
null for every other kind.

DiffLineKind.description: The kind of one line of a line diff between two artifact versions (FR-21).

DriftAreaDto.description: A drift area reported by the review agent (§4.7).

EventOutcome.description:
Whether an event records something going wrong (FR-51 admin event log "status" filter). Events are append-only facts
with no delivery status of their own, so the admin log filters on this outcome instead.

EvidenceDto.description: Why the review agent scored a category as it did: a file (when the evidence points at one) and the reason.

ExecutionCountsDto.description: Step counts of the current plan version.

ExecutionPlanDto.description: The plan version the steps belong to.

ExecutionRunDto.description:
One execution run (FR-57): the steps of one plan version. `id` is the plan artifact's id. The development run is
the implementation plan's; a review-fix run is the optimisation plan of review `cycle`. A run of an invalidated
plan is `superseded` (status `superseded`, with `supersededReason`). `tokens` is input + output
tokens of the steps' agent runs; `commitCount` the steps committed. `complianceReportId` is the report whose
optimisation plan this is (null for the development run): cycle numbers restart after a rollback, report ids don't.

ExecutionRunStatus.description:
The execution runner's overall state for a project (FR-31, FR-33, FR-37): `idle` (not started, or nothing to run),
`running`, `paused` (no new step starts; a running step may still finish), `completed` (every step of the
current plan completed) or `blocked` (a step is blocked awaiting an escalation decision).

ExecutionStateDto.description:
The execution runner's state after a start/pause/resume request (FR-31, FR-37). `paused` is the project's pause flag;
`currentStepNumber` is the step `in_progress`, if any; `counts` are over the current plan version's steps.

ExecutionStepDto.description:
One execution step of a plan version (FR-30–FR-34): the plan step (number, title, task, declared files, dependencies on
earlier step numbers, user instructions) and its progress — status, attempt, the last attempt's violations, and the
branch and commit once accepted. `commitUrl` links the commit on GitHub; it is `null` for the Local provider
(no remote) and before the step is committed.

ExecutionStepSummaryDto.description:
One step of an execution run (FR-57): number, title, the specialist that runs it (`agentKey`, FR-121; null for the
base Code Generator), status, attempt count, declared vs produced files, and the commit once accepted
(`commitUrl` is null for the Local provider). `legacyAgentKey` (§4.23): the v2 agent key a plan locked before
the upgrade named, which now runs as `agentKey`; null otherwise.

ExecutionStepsDto.description: A plan version's execution steps in step order (FR-30); `plan` is `null` (and no steps) before any plan is approved.

ExternalCheckDto.description:
FR-85: a GitHub check run or commit status on the PR head as review saw it. `conclusion` is `null` for a check
still pending when review stopped waiting. A failed `required` check is a major `testing` finding.

ExternalChecksDto.description:
The external inputs a review cycle collected (FR-85, FR-89): the PR head's `checks`, how long review waited for
pending checks (`checksWaitedSeconds`, up to 15 minutes; `null` when it didn't wait) and whether it gave up
waiting (`checksTimedOut`, recorded as a warning). `preview` is the preview deployment review waited for
(FR-90; `null` when none, e.g. Vercel not configured).

ExternalDatabaseRequest.description: FR-152: an External database's connection string (`postgres://`, `postgresql://` or ADO.NET), stored encrypted and never returned.

FileAction.description: Declared action for a file in a plan step (FR-29).

FileManifestEntryDto.description: A file an accepted step wrote (FR-34), with the SHA-256 of its content.

FindingSource.description: Where a review violation came from (§4.7): a deterministic check or the Code Review agent.

GateDto.description:
An approval gate (§4.2, FR-12–FR-15). `artifactId`, `artifactType` and `artifactVersion` identify
the gated artifact (spec and plan gates). Escalation gates carry `escalationReason` and, once decided,
`decision` (and `targetCheckpoint` for a rollback; D-V2-11: was `targetVersion`). `reason` is a human-readable context line.
`decidedBy`, `decidedAt` and `comment` are set once the gate is decided. `overdue` is true
72 hours after creation while pending (FR-15); `remindedAt` is when its 24-hour reminder was sent. An escalation raised by a blocked execution step (FR-33) has
`escalationReason` `step_blocked` and names the step in `executionStepId` and `stepNumber`
(both `null` otherwise). `releaseVersionId` is the release version the gate belongs to (§4.10).

GitBindingDto.description:
The Git connection bound to a GitLab or Bitbucket project (FR-136), shown to Owners as e.g. "GitLab · connected by Ana
(@ana)". Never contains a token. `connectionId` only lets the binding Owner recognise their own connection.

GitBindingUserDto.description: The Owner who bound a project's Git connection (FR-136).

GitConnectionAuthKind.description: How a GitConnection authenticates (FR-131, FR-134). Wire values: `oauth`, `token`.

GitConnectionStatus.description:
State of a GitConnection (FR-131, FR-134). Wire values: `valid`, `invalid`,
            `insufficient_scope`.

GitHostInstanceRefDto.description: A Git host instance as project settings show it (FR-136).

GitHostInstanceSource.description: Where a GitLab instance's settings come from (FR-130). Wire values: `database`, `configuration`.

GitHubAppManifestDto.description:
A GitHub App manifest (FR-80, §4.14), in GitHub's own field names so the page can post it unchanged (as the
`manifest` form field, JSON-encoded): name `AIDE ({host})` (the host of `App:PublicBaseUrl`); `url` and `setup_url` under
`App:PublicBaseUrl`; `redirect_url` the manifest callback (`/api/admin/integrations/github/callback`);
`callback_urls` the sign-in callback (`/api/auth/github/callback`); no `hook_attributes` (GitHub rejects a
localhost webhook URL even when inactive, and needs a URL whenever the object is present), so the App has no webhook; private; and
`default_permissions` contents, pull_requests, workflows, administration and pages (FR-143) `write`, metadata, checks and
statuses `read` (the Admin may drop `administration`, which disables "Create repository"); no events.

GitHubAppManifestResponseDto.description:
What the page posts to GitHub (FR-80): an HTML form `POST` to `postUrl`
(`https://github.com/settings/apps/new?state=…`, or
`https://github.com/organizations/{org}/settings/apps/new?state=…`) with the field `manifest` set to the
JSON of `manifest`. `state` (also in `postUrl`) is single-use, bound to the Admin's session and checked
by the callback.

GitHubAppStatus.description: Whether the AIDE GitHub App is registered (FR-80). Wire values: `not_configured`, `configured`.

GitHubConnectionDto.description:
The caller's GitHub connection (FR-81). Tokens are never returned. When `connected` is false, `login`,
`githubUserId`, `status` and `accessExpiresAt` are `null` and `installations` is empty.
`status` is `invalid` after a failed token refresh (§4.14); `accessExpiresAt` is `null` when the
App's tokens don't expire. `installUrl` is the App's "Install AIDE on more repositories" link (`null` when no
App is registered).

GitHubInstallationDto.description:
An installation of the AIDE GitHub App that the caller can access (FR-81, `GET /user/installations`):
`repositorySelection` is `all` or `selected`; `manageUrl` is where the user adds repositories to it.
`pagesPermission` (FR-143) is whether the installation grants the App's Pages write permission (`granted`,
`missing`: the Owner has to accept the updated permissions on the installation, or `unknown`).

GitHubOwnerDto.description:
A possible owner for "Create repository" (FR-81): the caller (`user`) or an organisation they belong to.
`appInstalled` / `installationId`: whether (and where) the AIDE GitHub App is installed on it;
`canCreate`: the App is installed, has Administration write, and (for an organisation) the caller may create
repositories there.

GitHubOwnerType.description: Owner kind of a GitHub App (FR-80). Wire values: `user`, `organization`.

GitHubPagesAccess.description:
FR-143: whether GitHub reports the AIDE App's Pages permission. Wire values: `granted`, `missing`,
            `unknown`.

GitHubReleaseDto.description: A GitHub release (FR-73 import, FR-86): `isLatest` marks GitHub's latest release.

GitHubRepoDto.description:
A repository the AIDE GitHub App can access for the caller (FR-81, FR-86). `installationId` is the installation
that grants it (send it with `repoFullName` in `POST /api/projects`). `empty` is whether the repo has
no commits (`null`: not checked in the list; `GET …/refs` always says). `canPush`: the caller may push to it
(push, maintain or admin); only such repositories can back a project (FR-82, FR-83).

GitHubRepoPageDto.description: A page of the repo picker (FR-81): `hasMore` is true when `page + 1` has more repositories.

GitHubRepoRefsDto.description:
What the wizard needs to know about a picked repository (FR-73, FR-86): its default branch, whether it is
`empty` (no commits: "start from scratch"; otherwise it is treated as an import), its releases and tags.

GitHubRepositorySelection.description: Which repositories an App installation covers (FR-81). Wire values: `all`, `selected`.

GitHubSignInMode.description:
How "Continue with GitHub" signs in (D-V2-7). Wire values: `app` (the App's user authorization flow with
            PKCE), `oauth` (the v1 OAuth App, only while no App is registered), `none` (GitHub sign-in unavailable).

GitHubTagDto.description:
A tag; `semver` is its version (a leading `v` or the tag prefix stripped), or `null` when the
    tag isn't a semantic version.

GitLabConnectionDto.description:
A GitLab connection of the caller (FR-131); never a token. `authKind` is `oauth` or `token` (access token
fallback); `scopes` as granted or validated; `expiresAt` is an access token's own expiry, and
`expiryWarning` is true from 14 days before it. `status`: `valid`, `invalid` (GitLab rejected it; reconnect)
or `insufficient_scope`. `instanceEnabled: false` means an Admin disabled the instance ("GitLab instance disabled").

GitLabInstanceSummaryDto.description:
An enabled GitLab instance for users (sign-in, connections). `oauthConfigured`: "Continue with GitLab" and
    "Connect with GitLab" are offered; otherwise only the token fallback.

GitLabOwnerDto.description:
Where the caller can create a GitLab project (FR-132): their personal namespace (`kind: user`) and the groups where
they are at least Developer (`kind: group`). `canCreateProjects` follows the group's
`project_creation_level`; `reason` says why not. Pass `fullPath` as `owner` when creating.

GitLabOwnerKind.description: A place a GitLab project can be created (FR-132). Wire values: `user`, `group`.

GitLabPendingLinkDto.description:
FR-131 sign-in: GitLab's verified email belongs to an existing AIDE account that isn't linked to this GitLab identity.
AIDE never links silently: the user signs in to that account (any method) and confirms with
`POST /api/auth/gitlab/link`, or cancels with `DELETE /api/auth/gitlab/link`. Expires after 10 minutes.

GitLabReleaseDto.description: A GitLab Release (FR-141): `isLatest` marks the newest released one (upcoming releases aren't listed).

GitLabRepoDto.description:
A GitLab project for the repo picker (FR-132). `id` is GitLab's numeric project id as text; `fullPath`
    is `group/sub/project`.

GitLabRepoPageDto.description: One page of projects (30, newest first); pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` for the next (`null` = last page).

GitLabRepoRefsDto.description:
What the wizard needs about a picked GitLab repository (FR-141, FR-86): its canonical path, default branch, whether it
is `empty` (no commits, or only starter files), its Releases and tags, and the import's suggestion: the released
version to preselect (the latest release, else the highest release, else the highest semver tag; `null` = "Never
released") and the version to develop it prefills (its next minor, else `0.1.0`).

GitLabTagDto.description: A tag; `semver` is its version (the `v` prefix stripped), or `null` when it isn't a semantic version.

GitLabVersionVerdict.description: The outcome of a GitLab `GET /api/v4/version` reachability check (FR-130).

GitProvider.description:
Git provider of a project (FR-35, FR-82, FR-136). Wire values: `github_pat` (v1 `github`), `local`,
            `github_app`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`.

oneOf.description: FR-136: the Git host instance of a GitLab or Bitbucket project (`null` otherwise).

externalRepoId.description: FR-136: the host's repo id (GitLab project id, Bitbucket repository UUID).

repoWebUrl.description: The repository's web URL (GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket), `null` for Local.

oneOf.description:
FR-136: the binding ("GitLab · connected by Ana (@ana)"); `null` when the project isn't on GitLab/Bitbucket or
the binding was cleared (Git work then fails with `GIT_NOT_CONNECTED` until an Owner re-binds).

canRebind.description: FR-136: the caller may re-bind their own connection (`connectionId`): an Owner of a GitLab or Bitbucket project.

GitSettingsDto.description:
Git settings (FR-9, FR-35, FR-82, FR-83). The token is never returned, only `hasToken`. `branchName` is the
project branch, once the working copy has been prepared. `mode` is the v2 name of `provider` (always equal).
For `github_app`, `installationId`, `repoId` and `repoFullName` identify the repo (else
`null`). `appInstalledOnRepo` says whether the AIDE GitHub App can access a `github_pat` project's repo
(`null`: not checked, no App, or not a PAT project); `canSwitchToApp` is true when it can and the caller is an
Owner ("Switch to GitHub App"). `mergeStrategy` (FR-65: `aide_merges`, the default, or `manual`) and
`tagPrefix` (§4.10, FR-64: default `v`, so tags read `v1.2.0`) are the project's release settings.

GitTestResultDto.description: Result of testing the saved Git settings (FR-10); `reason` says why when `ok` is false.

errorCode.description: Stable UPPER_SNAKE error code from the spec's error table (SPEC §6).

traceId.description: Trace id for correlating the error with server logs.

details.description: Individual reasons, when there are several.

reason.description: Machine-readable sub-reason for some codes. RESTORE_NOT_ALLOWED: stage_completed, stage_not_reached, other_release_version, corrupted or releasing.

installUrl.description: GITHUB_APP_NOT_INSTALLED: the AIDE GitHub App's install link, when an App is registered (FR-81, FR-83). PLATFORM_GIT_NOT_CONNECTED: the platform's Git install or connect link; PLATFORM_PERMISSION_MISSING: the AIDE GitHub App's settings link (FR-143, FR-144).

platform.description: PLATFORM_GIT_NOT_CONNECTED, PLATFORM_PLAN_LIMIT, PLATFORM_PERMISSION_MISSING, PLATFORM_ERROR: the platform (vercel, netlify, cloudflare, render, railway, github_pages, fake) for the copy's {platform} (FR-144, D-V4-4).

layer.description: The choice: frontend, backend, data, vcs, frontendHost, backendHost, databaseHost, local or originModel.

option.description: The option id that breaks the rule.

JobDto.description: A background job (§4.9): the job queued by a dead-letter retry (FR-51).

LegacyPresetDto.description:
FR-129: the retired v2 preset a migrated version was pinned to, kept as history: its id, name (the id when unknown),
version and `label`, "Preset nextjs-supabase@1.0.1 (retired, migrated)".

LinkDeploymentResourceRequest.description: FR-144: link an existing platform resource (from `GET /api/me/connections/platforms/:id/resources`).

LlmBindingDto.description:
The connection bound to a project (FR-79), shown to every member as e.g. "Anthropic · connected by Ana (••••a1b2)".
Never contains the key. `credentialId` only lets the binding Owner recognise their own connection; nobody else can
bind it (`CREDENTIAL_NOT_OWNER`).

LlmBindingUserDto.description: The Owner who bound a project's LLM connection (FR-79).

LlmBoundProjectDto.description: A project that has an LLM connection bound (FR-79).

LlmConnectionsDto.description:
The caller's LLM connections, newest first (FR-78), and `keylessProviders`: the providers that need no key and
are always available (Ollama at the system base URL, and Fake), when enabled on this deployment (FR-157).

LlmCredentialDto.description:
One of the caller's LLM connections (FR-78). The key is never returned: only the provider, label, its last 4
characters, the validation status (`valid`, `invalid`, `unchecked`) and when it was last checked, plus
the projects it is bound to. `last4` is `????` for a key migrated from v1 until the start-up backfill reads it.

LlmCredentialStatus.description: Validation state of an LLM credential (FR-78). Wire values: `valid`, `invalid`, `unchecked`.

LlmModelDto.description:
A model of a provider's catalog (FR-158, §4.24): id, display name, max output tokens per call, context window and
    whether it's recommended.

LlmProviderConnectionDto.description: One of the caller's LLM connections for a provider (FR-78, FR-158): never the key, only its last 4 characters.

LlmProviderDto.description:
An LLM provider enabled on this deployment, as seen by the caller (FR-158). `usable` and `reason`
(`system_key`, `own_connection`, `keyless`, `needs_connection`) say whether the caller can choose it
now; `connections` are the caller's own connections for it (newest first); `catalog` is its model catalog and
`defaultModel` the system default model (`Llm:Providers:<P>:DefaultModel`). `isDefault` (FR-159) is true
on the one provider a project created now by the caller without an LLM choice would get (§4.24
`DefaultForNewProject`), false on all others (all false when that rule yields `LLM_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`).

LlmProviderReason.description:
Why an enabled LLM provider is or isn't usable by a user (FR-158, §4.24). Wire values: `system_key`,
`own_connection`, `keyless`, `needs_connection`.

LlmProviderStatusDto.description: Whether a provider can be used: an allowed system key is configured or the project has a bound connection for it (Ollama and Fake are always configured).

LlmSettingsDto.description:
LLM settings (FR-9, FR-22, FR-79). Keys are never returned. `hasApiKey` is true while a connection is bound
(kept from v1); `binding` describes it (`null` when nothing is bound). `canBind` is true when the caller
is a project Owner and so may bind one of their own connections or unbind. `providers` lists every provider with
whether it's usable and its system default model; only providers enabled on this deployment are listed (FR-157).

ManagedDatabaseProvider.description: Where a managed database lives (§5). Wire values: `supabase`, `render`, `railway`, `external`, `fake`.

MergeReadinessDto.description:
FR-84 merge readiness of the version's PR, as of `checkedAt`. `canMerge` is whether AIDE's token may merge it
now (repository permission and allowed merge methods, branch rules, the PR's `mergeStateStatus` and
`reviewDecision`, required checks). `willAutoMerge` is `canMerge` under the `aide_merges` strategy
("AIDE will merge automatically"); otherwise "A merge on GitHub will be needed" with `reasons` (empty when
`canMerge`, except `manual_strategy`). `checks` are the PR head's check runs and commit statuses.
`mergeStateStatus` and `reviewDecision` are GitHub's GraphQL values verbatim (e.g. `CLEAN`,
`BLOCKED`; `APPROVED`, `REVIEW_REQUIRED`), `null` when unknown. For a GitLab project (FR-138)
`mergeStateStatus` is the merge request's `detailed_merge_status` verbatim (e.g. `mergeable`,
`not_approved`), `reviewDecision` is `null` and `checks` are the head's pipeline jobs and commit
statuses (FR-139). For a Local project
`canMerge` is true with no checks. The merge itself stays authoritative (FR-65).

MergeReadinessReasonCode.description:
FR-84: why AIDE can't merge the version's PR itself (wire values `review_required`, `changes_requested`,
`checks_failing`, `checks_pending`, `branch_protected`, `merge_conflict`, `no_permission`,
`merge_method_not_allowed`, `pr_not_open`, `manual_strategy`), plus FR-138's GitLab/Bitbucket reasons
`draft`, `discussions_unresolved` and `rebase_required`. Also recorded on an `awaiting_merge`
release attempt (FR-65).

MergeReadinessReasonDto.description: FR-84: one reason AIDE can't merge the version's PR itself, with copy for the Release page and the gate.

MergeStrategy.description:
FR-65 merge strategy. Wire values: `aide_merges`, `manual`; FR-140 (Bitbucket only): `fast_forward` and
`squash`, which are `aide_merges` with Bitbucket's `merge_strategy` of that name (`aide_merges` sends
`merge_commit`).

MigrationFileDto.description: One file a migration run applied: version, name and duration (ms).

MigrationRunDto.description:
FR-153, §7 Migrations page: one Supabase BaaS migration run: environment, database, release and version, commit, status
(`running`, `succeeded`, `failed`), the files applied with durations, the total duration, the error
(`MIGRATION_FAILED`, `MIGRATION_HISTORY_DIVERGED`) and the advisor findings.

MigrationRunStatus.description: A migration run's state (§5). Wire values: `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`.

NotificationChannelDto.description:
A notification channel (FR-47). Secrets are never returned, only `hasSecret`. For `email` and
`webhook`, `target` is the saved address or URL and the secret is a webhook's HMAC signing key. For
`slack` and `teams`, the incoming-webhook URL is itself the secret (a bearer credential): it is stored
encrypted, `target` is only a masked display value (host only, e.g. `hooks.slack.com/…`) and
`hasSecret` is `true` once a URL is saved.

id.description: The id of an existing channel to keep (its secret, or Slack/Teams URL, is kept unless a new one or `clearSecret` is sent, or the type changes); omit for a new channel.

target.description:
Email address (email) or https URL (webhook); required for both. For slack and teams the URL is sent in
`secret` and `target` may be omitted or echo the masked value; an absolute URL sent here is still
accepted as the incoming-webhook URL (older clients) and treated as a secret.

secret.description:
The channel secret, stored encrypted and never returned: the HMAC signing key (webhook) or the https
incoming-webhook URL (slack, teams). Required for a new webhook, slack or teams channel; omit it to keep the saved
one of the same channel (same id and type). Webhook, slack and teams channels can't clear it without sending a new
one. Email channels have none.

NotificationChannelInput.description: A channel in a notification settings update.

NotificationDto.description:
An in-app notification of the caller (FR-47). `projectId` and `projectName` are `null` for
notifications not tied to a project (or whose project was deleted). `link` is a relative app page path (e.g.
`/projects/<id>`, `/projects/<id>/runs` or `/projects/<id>/artifacts/<type>`); it never
carries an approval token (one-click approval links go only to project channels). `readAt` is `null` while unread.

NotificationEvent.description:
Events a notification channel can subscribe to (FR-47, FR-92). Wire values are snake_case and equal the notification
types (`NotificationRules.ChannelTypes`); the personal `connection_invalid` never goes to project channels.

NotificationPageDto.description:
A page of the caller's notifications, newest first. `unreadCount` counts all the caller's unread notifications
(not just this page). Load more with `before` = `nextBefore`; `null` on the last page.

NotificationPreferencesDto.description:
The caller's in-app notification preferences (§2): notification types they don't want in their notification centre.
Project channels (email, Slack, Teams, webhook) are configured per project by Owners, not here.

NotificationType.description:
The kind of an in-app notification (FR-47, FR-15). The project channel events (`NotificationEvent`) plus
`gate_reminder`, the 24-hour reminder of a pending gate, and the personal `connection_invalid` (FR-92).
Wire values are snake_case.

PagedResultOfAdminAgentRunDto.description: One page of results. int PagedResult<T>.Page is 1-based.

PagedResultOfAdminEventDto.description: One page of results. int PagedResult<T>.Page is 1-based.

PagedResultOfAdminUserDto.description: One page of results. int PagedResult<T>.Page is 1-based.

PagedResultOfAgentRunDto.description: One page of results. int PagedResult<T>.Page is 1-based.

PagedResultOfDeadLetterDto.description: One page of results. int PagedResult<T>.Page is 1-based.

PagedResultOfProjectSummaryDto.description: One page of results. int PagedResult<T>.Page is 1-based.

Phase.description: The six lifecycle phases, in order (§4.1). Stored as snake_case strings.

PlanRunStatus.description:
The state of one execution run (FR-57): the steps of one plan version. `pending` (no step started),
`running`, `paused`, `completed` (every step completed), `blocked` (a step awaits an escalation
decision) or `superseded` (the plan was invalidated; its run stays listed under "Superseded").

PlatformAccountDto.description:
A team, account, workspace or organisation a platform token reaches (FR-142): its id (send it as `accountId`),
name, slug (Vercel teams, Netlify accounts, Supabase organisations) and kind (e.g. `team`, `user`,
`workspace`, `organization`; `null` when the platform doesn't say).

PlatformBoundProjectDto.description: A project whose deployment target is bound to a platform connection (FR-144).

PlatformConnectionDto.description:
One of the caller's platform connections (FR-142). The token is never returned: only the label and its last 4
characters. `accountId`/`accountName` are the account it is for (the Vercel or Netlify user or team, Cloudflare
account, Render workspace, Railway workspace, Supabase organisation; `null` when not chosen or unknown),
`metadata` what else the token reaches, `scopes` its scopes where the platform reports them, `expiresAt`
its expiry (`null`: none or unknown), `status` (`valid`, `invalid`, `insufficient_scope`,
`unchecked`) and when it was last checked, plus the projects whose deployment targets are bound to it.

PlatformConnectionMetadataDto.description:
What the platform says about a token (FR-142). `teamId`/`teamSlug`: a team-scoped Vercel token's team.
`accounts`: the teams, accounts, workspaces or organisations it reaches. `policies`: a Cloudflare token's
permission groups (empty when the token can't read them). `missingPermissions`: what the platform said is missing
(Supabase `missing_permissions`; non-empty with status `insufficient_scope`). `tokenKind`: e.g. Railway
`workspace` or `account`, Cloudflare `user` (`null` when it doesn't matter).

PlatformConnectionStatus.description:
Validation state of a platform connection (FR-142). Wire values: `valid`, `invalid` (rejected),
            `insufficient_scope` (missing permissions), `unchecked`.

PlatformProvider.description:
Deployment platforms and databases with pasted-token connections (FR-142, §4.20, §4.21). Wire values:
            `vercel`, `netlify`, `cloudflare`, `render`, `railway`, `supabase`.

PlatformResourceDto.description:
An entry of a platform picker (FR-142 `GET …/resources`): the platform's id (send it as the resource to link), its
name, URL when there is one, and a short detail (e.g. the linked repository, the service type, a project's region and
status).

PreviewCheckDto.description:
FR-90: the preview deployment a review cycle waited for (`compliance_report.external_checks.preview`): its id, final
(or last seen) `status`, `url` and `buildLogTail`, how long review waited (`waitedSeconds`, up to 20
minutes; `null` when it didn't wait) and whether it gave up waiting (`timedOut`).

errorCode.description: Stable UPPER_SNAKE error code from the spec's error table (SPEC §6).

traceId.description: Trace id for correlating the error with server logs.

details.description: Individual reasons, when there are several.

reason.description: Machine-readable sub-reason for some codes. RESTORE_NOT_ALLOWED: stage_completed, stage_not_reached, other_release_version, corrupted or releasing.

installUrl.description: GITHUB_APP_NOT_INSTALLED: the AIDE GitHub App's install link, when an App is registered (FR-81, FR-83). PLATFORM_GIT_NOT_CONNECTED: the platform's Git install or connect link; PLATFORM_PERMISSION_MISSING: the AIDE GitHub App's settings link (FR-143, FR-144).

platform.description: PLATFORM_GIT_NOT_CONNECTED, PLATFORM_PLAN_LIMIT, PLATFORM_PERMISSION_MISSING, PLATFORM_ERROR: the platform (vercel, netlify, cloudflare, render, railway, github_pages, fake) for the copy's {platform} (FR-144, D-V4-4).

layer.description: The choice: frontend, backend, data, vcs, frontendHost, backendHost, databaseHost, local or originModel.

option.description: The option id that breaks the rule.

ProjectDto.description:
A project as shown on its overview and settings pages (FR-5, FR-7). `myRole` is the caller's project role (`null`
for an Admin who isn't a member); a `null` `tokenBudget` means unlimited. `checkpoint` is the lifecycle
checkpoint within the current release version `releaseVersionId` (§4.10, D-V2-11: was `projectVersion`);
`releasedVersion` is the highest released version (`null`: not released) and `developmentVersion` the
version in development (`null`: none) (FR-62). `idea` is the request of the version in development.
`presetId`, `presetName` and `presetVersion` are history (FR-129): the retired v2 preset the current release
version was pinned to before it was migrated to a composition (all `null`: never pinned to a preset). `deploymentsEnabled`: the project has deployment settings (FR-88), so
the Deployments page is in its navigation (§7.2). `stackPacks` are the pack ids of the current release version's
stack composition (FR-117, §5; empty: no stack), e.g. `["fe-react-vite", "be-aspnet", "vcs-github"]`.

category.description: Categories of project events, used to filter the activity feed (FR-50) and to group live updates (FR-46).

ProjectEventMessage.description:
A project event pushed live to everyone viewing the project (FR-46): the SignalR `projectEvent` message.
`id`, `type`, `payload` and `createdAt` are the stored audit event (FR-50); `category` tells the
page which data to refresh. Not an HTTP response: the schema is added to the OpenAPI components by
LiveContractDocumentTransformer so the generated client has the type.

ProjectKpisDto.description:
§7.2: the projects-list KPI row, over the projects matching the list's filters. `active`: not `released` (any
phase, including rolled back); `inReview`: status `reviewing`; `awaitingGates`: pending gates across
those projects; `released`: status `released`; `total`: the projects counted.

ProjectSettingsDto.description: All project settings with secrets as set / not set flags (FR-9).

ProjectSource.description: FR-73: where a new project's code comes from (wizard step "Source").

ProjectStackDto.description:
Settings → Stack (FR-117, FR-119): the stack of the project's current release version.
    * composition: the pinned normalised composition with its derived fields (§4.18), null for "No stack
    (general)" and, for a version migrated from a retired v2 preset, that preset as history (legacyPreset). catalogVersion/catalogHash are
    what it was pinned against; currentCatalogVersion/currentCatalogHash the catalog shipped now (a new
    version re-pins to it).
* locked with lockedReason (plan_locked, not_in_development): PUT is
    STACK_LOCKED then.
* stackChange: the layers that differ from the stack the version's base code was built with, and whether
    that is a stack change (the base commit has code: an iteration or an import), for the stack-change warning.
* repoVcs: the VCS option fixed by the project's repository host (R5; null: a Local repository, any
    VCS).

ProjectStateDto.description:
Deterministic project state for the overview page and the CLI (§6 `/api/projects/:id/state`). `tokensUsed`
counts every agent run's tokens; a `null` `tokenBudget` means unlimited (FR-26). `executionStatus` is the
execution runner's state over the current plan (FR-31, FR-37). `pullRequest` is the project PR once AIDE has opened
it (FR-36), else `null`. `latestRelease` is the latest release attempt of the current release version (FR-42,
FR-43), else `null`. Artifacts, steps, review and gates are those of the current release version
`releaseVersionId` (the version in development, else the latest released; §4.10). `checkpoint` was
`projectVersion` (D-V2-11). `suggestedNextVersion` prefills "Start new version" (FR-60: the next minor of the
released version). `latestDeployment` is the project's newest deployment of any target (FR-90, FR-91; `null`:
