none), for the overview and `aide status`. `productionUrls` (FR-151) is the production URL of each component
with a deployment target: the target's production URL (its stable domain), else the URL of the deployment production serves now.

ProjectStatus.description: Project status (§4.1: status follows phase; `released`, `rolled_back` and `awaiting_merge` are special).

ProjectSummaryDto.description:
A row of the projects list (FR-6, FR-62). `myRole` is `null` for an Admin who isn't a member;
`releasedVersion` / `developmentVersion` are the two version badges (`null` when not released / nothing in
development); `checkpoint` was `projectVersion` (D-V2-11); `presetId`/`presetName`/`presetVersion`
are history (FR-129: the retired preset the current version was migrated from; `null`: none); `stackPacks` the pack ids of the current version's
stack composition (FR-117, the `pack` filter; empty: no stack).

PullRequestCommitDto.description: A commit on the project branch that isn't on the default branch; `url` links it on GitHub (`null` for Local).

PullRequestDto.description:
The project PR with its branch comparison (FR-35, FR-36), read live from the working copy: the commits (newest first, at
most 250) and changed files (at most 1000; `truncated` when either list was cut). `comparisonAvailable` is
`false` when the working copy or a branch is missing (then both lists are empty).

PullRequestFileDto.description: A file changed on the project branch since it left the default branch.

PullRequestFileStatus.description: How a file differs between the default branch and the project branch (lowercase on the wire, like every enum).

PullRequestSummaryDto.description:
The project PR once recorded (FR-36): provider, base (default) and head (project) branch, and for GitHub its number and
web URL (both `null` for Local, whose "PR" is the recorded branch comparison). `openedAt` is when AIDE last
opened or reused it.

PutDeploymentEnvRequest.description:
Create or replace a user environment variable (FR-88, FR-145): the value (up to 64 KB; encrypted, never returned), its
environments (`targets`: `preview`, `production`), whether it is sensitive, the components it applies to
(`appliesTo`, default `["frontend"]`) and whether it is public (default: the key has the frontend pack's public
prefix; a prefixed key is always public). A public variable that looks secret, or a key AIDE derives, is
`VALIDATION`.

PutManagedDatabaseRequest.description:
FR-152 (Owner): set the environment's database. `provider` must be the composition's database host (`fake`
also in Fake mode); exactly one of `create`, `link` (a resource id from the connection's picker) or
`external` (External only). `connectionId` is one of the caller's own platform connections (not for External).

ReadinessItemDto.description: One readiness checklist item (FR-144): a stable `id`, `state` (`ok`, `warning`, `error`, `na`), a message and an optional fix link.

ReadinessState.description: State of a readiness item (FR-144). Wire values: `ok`, `warning`, `error`, `na`.

RefinementAnswerDto.description: An answer given to the agent: `questionId` when it answered a question of a round, and the question text.

RefinementAnswerRequest.description:
An answer for the next refinement round (FR-27): `questionId` of a question from the latest round, or the
`question` text for anything else, and the `answer`.

RefinementDto.description:
The refinement page (FR-27): the latest project request version (`latestDraft`, without content — read it from
the artifacts API), the latest round and its status, and the clarifying questions of the latest completed round
(`questionsRunId`) with any answers already given. `codebaseSummary` is the Repository Analyst's state for
the version (FR-70). `rounds` (FR-55) is every round of the selected release version, newest first (at most
`50`, the latest), with the questions each asked and the answers they were given.

RefinementQuestionDto.description:
A clarifying question of the latest completed round (FR-27). `answer` is the answer already given for the next
round (while that round is queued or running, or after it failed), else `null`.

RefinementRoundDto.description:
One refinement round (FR-27): an idea refinement job and its agent run. `runId` is the run that produced (or will
produce) the draft — the corrective re-run when the first reply couldn't be read; the run appears under
`/runs/{runId}` once the job has started. `status` is `queued` until then. `trigger` says who started
it: a writer (`user_requested`), or a rejected or corrupted project request. A round that ended without a draft
because the project no longer allowed one (e.g. a release in progress) is `cancelled`, with the reason in `error`. `answers` and `feedback` are
what the agent was given; `draftArtifactId`/`draftVersion` the project request version it created.

RefinementRoundHistoryDto.description:
One round of the refinement history (FR-55, FR-27). `round` is its 1-based number within the release version
(oldest = 1). `startedAt` is when it was queued, `completedAt` when its run (or job) ended. `questions` are
the clarifying questions this round asked (empty unless it `succeeded`), each with the `answer` a later round
gave it (the latest round started before the next succeeded round, as on the page), else `null`. `answers` and
`feedback` are what this round's agent was given; `draftArtifactId`/`draftArtifactVersion` the project
request version it created.

password.description: At least 8 characters with a letter and a digit.

RegressionDto.description:
An `[unchanged]` requirement the review found broken in an iteration (§4.13): the requirement id, the category it
was reported under, what is broken and the evidence. Regressions carry no deterministic penalty.

ReleaseDto.description:
A release attempt (FR-42 amended by FR-64, FR-43) of release version `releaseVersionId`, approved at checkpoint
`checkpoint`. `status` is `in_progress` while the release job is queued or running, then
`succeeded` (merged into the default branch and tagged `tag`, `mergeCommitSha` set) or `failed`, or
`awaiting_merge` (FR-65) when the merge was refused or the strategy is `manual`: `awaitingMergeSince` is
when it started waiting and `mergeReasons` are the merge-readiness reasons (FR-84) recorded then (`null`
otherwise); the merge poll then completes it once the PR is merged on GitHub (§4.14).
A failed release carries `errorCode` (e.g. `MERGE_CONFLICT`) and `errorMessage`; on a merge conflict
`conflictingFiles` lists the files (empty otherwise). `pullRequestUrl` is the merged GitHub PR (`null`
for Local). `attempt` counts the release attempts at this checkpoint (1 for the first, +1 per retry).
`completedAt` is `null` while in progress. `tag` is the version's tag `<tagPrefix><version>`
(e.g. `v1.2.0`; v1 releases keep their `v<N>-aide` tag). A tag that already exists on another commit fails
the release with `TAG_EXISTS`. `mergeCommitSha` is set as soon as the merge exists, before tagging.
Failure codes include `MERGE_CONFLICT`, `TAG_EXISTS`, `GIT_ERROR`, `RELEASE_CANCELLED`,
`GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED`, and while awaiting the merge `PR_CLOSED` (closed without merging) and
`MERGE_TIMEOUT` (not merged within 14 days); after either the project stays in `release` and an Owner can
retry with `POST /release`. `githubReleaseUrl` is the host release created for the tag: the GitHub Release
(FR-64), the GitLab Release, or the Bitbucket annotated tag's page (FR-140; Bitbucket has no Releases); `null` for
Local or before it exists. AIDE's full release notes of a succeeded Bitbucket release (the tag's message, FR-140,
D-V4-7) are read with `GET …/releases/{releaseId}/notes`. A GitLab merge refused because the
merge request's head moved since review (409) fails with `GIT_ERROR`. `mergeStrategy` is the project's current merge strategy (FR-65).
`productionDeployment` is the release's production deployment (FR-91: the newest for this release attempt, including
redeploys; `null` when deployment isn't configured or not created yet). A failed one doesn't undo the release.

ReleaseNotesDto.description:
FR-140, D-V4-7: AIDE's full release notes of a release attempt, for a host without Releases (Bitbucket: the annotated
tag's message), rebuilt from the version's locked spec, completed steps and latest review; `null` for other hosts
or an attempt that hasn't succeeded.

ReleaseStatus.description: Outcome of a release attempt (FR-42, FR-43).

ReleaseSummaryDto.description:
The latest release attempt in the project state (FR-42, FR-43, FR-64, FR-65): enough for the overview's release banner,
including "Awaiting merge" with the PR link and reasons, and the GitHub Release link. Fields as in `ReleaseDto`.

ReleaseVersionCheckpointsDto.description:
The lifecycle checkpoints of a release version (§4.10): `current` is the project's checkpoint for the version in
development (or the latest checkpoint recorded for any other version); `max` the highest checkpoint recorded in it
(above `current` after a rollback).

ReleaseVersionDto.description:
A release version of a project (§4.10, FR-60–FR-62). `version` is the normalised semver (no leading `v`);
`tag` is the release tag once released (or the imported/migrated tag, e.g. v1's `v7-aide`); `baseTag` and
`baseCommitSha` are the released tag and merge commit the version started from (null for a first version);
`branchName` and `pullRequestUrl` are the version's working branch and PR once they exist; `request` is
what the version was started with (the project idea for a first version); `startedBy` is null for versions created
by migration or import. `presetId`/`presetVersion`/`presetName` are history (FR-129): the retired v2 preset
the version was pinned to before its migration to a composition, shown as "Preset <id>@<version> (retired,
migrated)"; all `null` for versions never pinned to a preset.

ReleaseVersionStatus.description: Status of a release version (§4.10). Wire values: `in_development`, `awaiting_merge`, `released`, `imported`.

ReportPlanDto.description: The optimisation plan a review cycle produced (FR-40): its artifact id, version and status.

ReviewRunStatus.description: The review job's state for the project (FR-38): no review in the current cycle, queued or running, finished, or failed.

ReviewStartedDto.description: A review was queued (FR-38): the review job's id and the cycle number the review will record.

ReviewStateDto.description: Review cycle progress and the latest compliance result (FR-38). `maxCycles` includes extra cycles granted by escalations (FR-14 continue). `status` is the review job's state: `running` while a review is queued or running, then `completed` or `failed`; `idle` before the first cycle or after a rollback cleared the review state (§4.8).

RollbackDto.description:
A recorded rollback (FR-44, §4.8): from checkpoint `fromCheckpoint` to `toCheckpoint` of release version
`releaseVersionId`, restoring `restoredPhase`. `invalidatedArtifactIds` are the artifacts created after the target checkpoint; `resetStepIds` the steps of
invalidated plans (now `invalidated`); `requeuedStepIds` the blocked or rejected steps of surviving plans
(back to `pending`); `cancelledGateIds` and `cancelledJobIds` the pending gates and queued jobs it
cancelled. `createdBy` is the Owner (or the system, for an escalation decision recorded by a worker).

RollbackRequest.description:
Roll the project back to an earlier checkpoint (FR-44, FR-63, §4.8, §4.10). `targetCheckpoint` must be below the
current checkpoint, recorded in the release version in development, and not a release-phase checkpoint; `reason` is
recorded on the rollback and its state transition.

RunInputArtifactDto.description: An artifact version a run used as input (FR-23).

Severity.description: Severity of a review finding or drift area (§4.7).

StackCatalogDto.description:
The stack catalog (FR-113, §4.16) for the wizard's Stack step, Settings → Stack and Admin → Stack catalog: the five
layers, the choices in evaluation order (frontend, backend, data, vcs, then the deployment choices frontendHost,
backendHost, databaseHost, local and originModel) with their options, the rule statements and the recommended
combinations. `version` and `contentHash` are what release versions pin.

StackCaveatDto.description: A caveat of a chosen option: the choice (`layer`), the option, the rule and its text.

StackChangeDto.description:
FR-117: `layersChanged` (catalog layers: `frontend`, `backend`, `data`, `vcs`, `deploy`)
against the stack the version's base code was built with; `isStackChange` when `baseHasCode` and a layer
changed (the spec then needs a "Stack Migration" section).

StackChoiceDto.description: A choice of the Stack step; `layer` is the layer it belongs to (the deployment choices share `deploy`).

StackChoiceStateDto.description:
A choice's options for the choices made so far: `selected` is the current selection, `default` the option to
preselect (R12 Compose, "same as frontend" for the backend host, the R10 origin model).

StackComponentSelection.description: A frontend or backend: the pack id (or `none`) and its path in the repo (FR-119; default `frontend`/`backend`).

StackCompositionRequest.description:
A (partial) composition (§4.17, §4.18). For `/options` a missing layer is "not chosen yet"; for `/validate` it
is None, except `vcs` (required), `deploy.local` (default: Compose when there's a backend or a database, R12)
and `originModel` (the default of R10). `"none"` as a pack or host is an explicit None.

StackDataSelection.description: The data layer: the pack id (or `none`); `mode` defaults to the option's (Supabase: `baas`).

StackDeployDto.description: Host option ids (`null` = None) and the local dev loop (`compose` or `none`).

StackDeploySelection.description: The Deployment layer: option ids of the frontend, backend and database hosts (or `none`) and the local dev loop (`compose`/`none`).

StackDerivedDto.description:
Derived facts (§4.18): the Next.js mode (R2), the specialists in play (FR-120), the origin models the Owner can switch
between (R10), and the selected packs' spec sections, env names and gate commands.

StackDetectedChoiceDto.description: A detected choice: the option id, the layer path (frontend, backend), the data mode and the evidence (e.g. "`next` 16.1 in `package.json`").

StackDetectionConflictDto.description: A choice whose matches disagree: left empty, with each candidate.

StackDetectionDto.description:
FR-118: the detected stack, to pre-fill the wizard's Stack step. `suggestions` are the detected choices (one per
choice id: `frontend`, `backend`, `data`, `vcs` — fixed to the repo's host —, `frontendHost`,
`backendHost`, `databaseHost`) with the layer path, the data mode and the evidence; `conflicts` are
choices left empty because matches disagree, with every candidate. Choices in neither list weren't detected.
`ref` and `commit` are what was read; `truncated`: the repository has more files than were listed.

StackLayerDto.description: One of the five layers (Frontend, Backend, Data, VCS, Deployment).

StackOptionDto.description:
An option card: name, one-line description, chips, and for pack options the pack id, its version
(`<plugin version>+aide.<n>`), its stack-packs source and its modes. `mode` is the pack mode the option
selects (Supabase: `baas`). Plain options (None, External, origin models) have no pack.

StackOptionState.description: §4.17: the state of an option for the choices made so far.

StackOptionStateDto.description: An option's state (`allowed`, `caveat`, `forbidden`, `invalidated`) with its reasons, and whether a recommended combination includes it.

StackOptionsDto.description:
`POST /api/stack/options` (§4.17): every choice in evaluation order with every option's state. A selection that
earlier choices now forbid is `invalidated` (the wizard clears it and names the reason); later choices are
evaluated without it. `nextjsMode` is R2's derived mode once known.

StackPackSourceDto.description: Where a pack was adapted from (FR-122): the stack-packs plugin, its version and the snapshot date.

StackReasonDto.description: A rule id (`R1`…) and its text, e.g. `R3` "Prisma needs Express, NestJS or Next.js full-stack".

StackRecommendationDto.description: A recommended combination (stack-packs `compose-stack`): option ids per choice id.

StackRuleDto.description: A compatibility rule (§4.17): its stable id (`R1`…) and statement.

StackVcsSelection.description: The VCS layer: the pack id, the GitLab host instance, and whether it is self-managed (R9).

StartRefinementRequest.description: Start a refinement round (FR-27), optionally answering some or all clarifying questions of the latest round.

oneOf.description: FR-117: the new version's stack composition (omitted: the base version's, re-pinned).

StartReleaseVersionRequest.description:
FR-60: start a new release version. `version` is semver (a leading `v` is stripped, e.g. `v1.2.0` →
`1.2.0`); `request` describes the new features, improvements or fixes and becomes the project idea for this
version. `stack` (FR-117,
"Change stack") is the new version's stack composition, validated like project create (`STACK_INCOMPATIBLE`,
`VCS_MISMATCH`, `VALIDATION` on `stack.*`); omitted or `null`, the base version's composition is kept,
re-pinned to the current catalog (`STACK_INCOMPATIBLE` if the catalog no longer allows it). FR-129: the v2
`presetId` was removed (D-V4-4).

StartReleaseVersionResultDto.description: FR-60: the release version that was started and the project state (now refinement / active at checkpoint 1).

StepAttemptDto.description:
One attempt of an execution step (FR-57): its outcome, the Guardian errors (`violations`) and `warnings`, the
files an accepted attempt committed, its agent run (null when the run row is gone) and that run's tool calls.

StepAttemptOutcome.description: Outcome of an execution step attempt (FR-57). Wire values: `accepted`, `rejected`, `error`.

StepAttemptRunDto.description: The agent run of a step attempt (FR-57): agent, specialist key, model, tokens, duration and status.

StepViolationDto.description: A Guardian violation recorded on a step's last rejected attempt (§4.6, FR-32). Never contains secret values.

ToolCallDto.description:
A repository tool call made during an agent run (FR-71): the tool name, its arguments as given by the model, the bytes
returned and whether the result was cut to the tool's limit. `error` is the code of a refused call
(`UNSAFE_PATH`, `TOOL_LIMIT`, `NOT_FOUND`, …), else `null`.

UnreadNotificationCountDto.description: The number of the caller's unread notifications (the bell badge).

UpdateBitbucketConsumerRequest.description:
Save the Bitbucket OAuth consumer (FR-133): its key (`clientId`) and secret. An omitted `clientSecret` keeps the
stored one (so the key can be corrected without re-entering the secret).

UpdateGitLabInstanceRequest.description:
Change a GitLab instance (FR-130); omitted fields are unchanged. An empty `clientId` or `clientSecret` clears it.
Changing `baseUrl` or `allowInsecureHttp` runs the SSRF guard and the reachability check again. gitlab.com's
base URL can't change. `enabled: false` disables the instance: its connections stop working and sign-in hides it.

oneOf.description:
`github_pat` or `local`. Moving onto `github_app` goes through
    `POST /settings/git/switch-to-app` (400 `VALIDATION` here).

repoUrl.description: Required when the provider is (or becomes) `github_pat`.

token.description: Sets the access token. To remove it, send `clearToken: true`.

connectionId.description:
FR-136: re-binds a GitLab or Bitbucket project to one of the caller's own connections on the project's instance
(Owner). AIDE first checks the connection's access to the repository: GitLab Developer or higher, Bitbucket
`write` or `admin` (else 403 `FORBIDDEN`). Another user's connection is 403 `CREDENTIAL_NOT_OWNER`;
an invalid one 409 `GIT_NOT_CONNECTED`; one on another instance, or `connectionId` on a project that isn't
on GitLab or Bitbucket, 400 `VALIDATION`.

oneOf.description:
FR-65: `aide_merges` (AIDE merges the PR on release) or `manual` (AIDE never merges; the release
    marks the PR ready for review and waits for the merge on the Git host). FR-140, Bitbucket projects only (else 400
    `VALIDATION`): `fast_forward` or `squash`, AIDE merging with that Bitbucket merge strategy
    (`aide_merges` merges with `merge_commit`); a project that leaves Bitbucket goes back to `aide_merges`.
    Applies to the next release attempt.

tagPrefix.description:
§4.10, FR-64: the tag prefix (`^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,20}$`, not starting with `.`, `/` or
    `-`; empty for bare `1.2.0` tags; else 400 `VALIDATION`). It also applies to the version in
    development. 409 `CONFLICT` while that version is `awaiting_merge` or a release attempt is in progress.

UpdateGitSettingsRequest.description: Partial update of the Git settings. Omitted fields are unchanged.

credentialId.description: The caller's connection to bind, or `null` to unbind. Omit it to keep the binding.

UpdateLlmSettingsRequest.description:
Partial update of the LLM settings (Owner). Omitted fields are unchanged; `modelsByAgent`, when sent, replaces the
map. FR-79: `credentialId` binds one of the caller's own connections for the (new) provider; `null` unbinds.
Changing the provider without sending `credentialId` drops a binding of the old provider. v1's per-project
`apiKey`/`clearApiKey` are gone: keys are added under Account → Connections (FR-78).

UpdateNotificationPreferencesRequest.description: Replaces the caller's muted notification types. An empty list mutes nothing.

tokenBudget.description: Sets the token budget (at least 1000). To remove the budget, send `clearTokenBudget: true`.

clearTokenBudget.description: `true` removes the token budget (unlimited). Can't be combined with `tokenBudget`.

UpdateProjectRequest.description: Partial update of a project (FR-7). Omitted fields are unchanged.

UserDto.description: The signed-in user (or a user, for admins).

ViolationDto.description: A violation found by a deterministic check or the review agent (§4.7). `file` and `evidence` are set when known.
